paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : GPQA confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how accuracy metrics vary as a function of binned initial confidence on GPQA, showing three series with error bars. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0.91 to 0.99 with regularly spaced tick labels at 0.01 intervals. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with major tick labels at approximately 0.2 increments. A blue solid line with circular markers (“Final Accuracy”) stays high across the range, starting near 0.91 at confidence 0.91, rising to about 1.00 at 0.93, dipping to about 0.86 at 0.96, then increasing again to around 0.97 at 0.98 before ending near 0.92 at 0.99. An orange dashed line with diamond markers (“Δ Accuracy”) begins around 0.55 at 0.91, reaches about 0.67 at 0.92, declines through roughly 0.47–0.48 at 0.93–0.94 and about 0.43 at 0.95, drops to around 0.28 at 0.96, rises to about 0.46 at 0.97, then falls sharply to about 0.10 at 0.98 and ends near 0.15 at 0.99. A green dash-dot line with square markers (“Initial Accuracy”) starts near 0.36 at 0.91, decreases to about 0.27 at 0.92, increases to about 0.53 at 0.93, stays around 0.48–0.52 at 0.94–0.95, rises to about 0.59 at 0.96, drops to around 0.42 at 0.97, increases to about 0.88 at 0.98, and ends near 0.77 at 0.99; all three series show vertical error bars with caps at each confidence bin.
